title: Rama's vow of refuge
hookLine: Ravana's own brother asks Rama for shelter, and Rama answers with a vow
carry: whoever comes once asking, god shelters
tomorrow: why would a mother ask God to look less like God?

lines: A KNOCK AT THE WORST HOUR.
cards: The knock always comes at the worst hour: a text near midnight, a friend on the step with a bag. Rama's comes on a beach.

His army is camped on the shore, facing Lanka, and a figure crosses the water through the air with a few companions and calls down. I'm Vibhishana, Ravana's brother. I told him to give Sita back, and he threw me out.
I've come to Rama for refuge. The whole camp goes quiet. The enemy's own brother is asking to come in.

teach.b: In Valmiki's Ramayana, Rama doesn't answer right away. He asks his allies. Sugriva, the monkey king, is wary: this could be a spy, here to learn the plans or strike while they sleep.
Others want to test him first, or keep him under guard until the war is won. Every one of those fears is reasonable; it is wartime, and he is Ravana's brother.

teach.h: A SPY? OR SOMEONE WHO MEANS IT?
teach.b: Hanuman speaks up for him: he chose his moment with care, and he talks like someone who means it. Then Rama answers, and the answer goes past the question.

teach.h: ANYONE WHO COMES ONCE, I PROTECT.
teach.b: Whoever comes to me even once, he says, and tells me they're mine, I protect from every being. That's my vow.
Then he goes further: even if Ravana himself came this way asking, I'd take him in. So Vibhishana is welcomed, and Rama has him anointed, right there, as the future king of Lanka.
Here's the part worth telling someone tonight. The camp was asking: is he safe for us? Rama answered a different question: who am I?

A refuge that only opens for the safe guest isn't much of a refuge. And a vow that has to be re-voted every night isn't much of a vow. This beach is the root of a big Hindu teaching: sharanagati, taking refuge.
Many Vaishnavas, Sri Vaishnavas above all, treasure Rama's vow as God's own promise. You don't earn your way in.

teach.h: SHARANAGATI: COME ONCE, AND BE HELD.
teach.b: Come once, honestly, say I'm yours, and you're held.

how: Sri Vaishnavas treasure Rama's vow of refuge to Vibhishana as one of their key verses on surrender, and the scene is played in Ram Lila performances.

o: the monkey king who warned that a spy had come
Ravana's brother, who fled Lanka across the sea
the prince who vowed refuge to anyone who comes asking

games.q: the night on the beach — tap the pairs.
p: wary: this could be a spy

s: Rama said yes without asking anyone
he asked his allies first and heard every doubt, then answered with his vow.
Rama said he'd take in even Ravana, if Ravana came asking
in Valmiki's telling the vow reaches the enemy himself.
Vibhishana was let in only after passing a test
some wanted a test; Rama answered with who he is, and had him anointed.

games.q: a friend says she's messed up too much for God to want her now. by Rama's vow on the beach, what's the true answer?
o: Rama's vow: whoever comes even once and asks is sheltered. no entry test.
first she has to make up for everything; then she can come back.
only people born into the right family get taken in.
games.why: Rama didn't ask Vibhishana for a clean record; he was Ravana's brother. sharanagati: coming, honestly, is enough.

practice: Fold your hands at your chest, the way Hindus do in front of a shrine: the gesture of someone who has come for refuge. If you pray, say Rama's name softly on each breath out, Ram, the way many Hindus repeat it through the day.
If you don't, let the folded hands say it for you: I've come, I'm here. Stay with that for the whole sit.

wordCard.voice: Rama: the prince of Ayodhya, in the Puranas Vishnu come as a man, whose vow was to shelter anyone who comes asking.

orig.note: Sanskrit sharanagati, coming for refuge: what Vibhishana does at Rama's camp.

carryVoice: Your line: whoever comes once asking, God shelters. That's sharanagati, and Rama said it would hold even for Ravana. Back tomorrow.

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 17–19 (Vibhishana arrives; the council; Rama's vow of refuge; Vibhishana anointed)
